did_you_know.text: Did you know? After Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.

Did you know? When the Israelites saw the fire and the glory of the LORD, they knelt and bowed facedown on the pavement of the courtyard and gave thanks, saying, “He is good; his mercy endures forever.”
Did you know? At the dedication of the temple, Solomon and all the people offered 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep.
Did you know? During the dedication ceremony, each group had its own role: the priests stood at their assigned posts, the Levites played musical instruments, and the priests blew the trumpets.
Did you know? Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard as a place for offering sacrifices because the bronze altar could not hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and fat portions.
Did you know? A very large crowd from all Israel attended the festival, from the region called Lebo Hamath in the north to the Wadi of Egypt in the south.
Did you know? After seven days of dedicating the altar and seven days of celebrating the festival, they held an assembly on the eighth day.
Did you know? Solomon sent the people home on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, and they returned joyful and glad because of the goodness the LORD had shown to David, Solomon, and Israel.

Did you know? The passage presents a sequence of repentance and restoration: the people humble themselves, pray, seek the LORD’s face, and turn from their evil ways; then the LORD hears, forgives, and heals the land.

Did you know? Alongside the promise that David’s dynasty would continue, the LORD warns that if Israel abandons his commands and worships other gods, they may be uprooted from the land, and the temple may become an object of ridicule and scorn.
